story.title: Investigation Requested into Juror in Lindsay Clancy Case
story.summary: Lindsay Clancy's attorney has filed a motion requesting the court to investigate a juror who was a holdout during her murder trial, which ended in a mistrial. The motion seeks to examine the juror's cellphone use during deliberations and assess the accuracy of his responses on pre-trial questionnaires and during questioning by the judge.

event_overview.title: About Lindsay Clancy Trial
event_overview.subject: Lindsay Clancy Trial
event_overview.summary: The Lindsay Clancy case is a Massachusetts criminal prosecution arising from the January 2023 deaths of Clancy’s three children in Duxbury. At trial, Clancy did not dispute causing the deaths; the central question was whether she was legally criminally responsible, with the defense asserting postpartum psychosis and the prosecution disputing that defense. The first trial ended without a verdict when the jury deadlocked.

facts.label: Underlying allegations and charges
facts.value: A Plymouth County grand jury indicted Lindsay Clancy over the January 24, 2023 deaths of her three children in Duxbury, Massachusetts. The Commonwealth charged three counts each of murder and strangulation.

facts.label: Court and jurisdiction
facts.value: The prosecution is a Commonwealth of Massachusetts case in Plymouth County Superior Court, within Massachusetts’s state criminal-court system.

facts.label: Core legal issue
facts.value: The trial concerned criminal responsibility rather than whether Clancy caused the children’s deaths: her defense sought a finding of not guilty by reason of insanity based on postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors argued she remained criminally responsible.

facts.label: First-trial outcome
facts.value: Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial on September 4, 2026, after the 12-person jury could not reach a unanimous verdict; therefore, the trial produced neither a conviction nor an acquittal.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline follows the late-July-to-early-September 2026 trial, deliberations, and mistrial, but does not attempt to cover the full 2023 investigation, all pretrial proceedings, or any later decision about retrial or dismissal.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the juror inquiry matter?
explore_lenses.title: It targets possible outside influence, not the verdict itself
explore_lenses.summary: Clancy’s defense is asking for a limited court inquiry into whether the holdout juror followed jury rules and accurately disclosed relevant information before being seated. That distinction matters because Massachusetts generally protects the substance of jurors’ deliberations, while allowing scrutiny of possible outside influences or misconduct.

claims.text: Massachusetts Trial Court policy prohibits jurors from using phones or other internet-capable devices while attending trial or deliberating, although devices may be used during lunch breaks if they are not used to obtain or disclose case-related information.

The defense motion seeks call and text records for the holdout juror during deliberation hours, along with preservation of court logs, video, juror questionnaires and related records; the request itself is not proof that improper phone use occurred.

Massachusetts evidence guidance bars juror testimony about deliberative statements, votes and mental processes, but permits inquiry concerning whether extraneous prejudicial information or an outside influence was improperly brought to bear.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case reach this dispute?
explore_lenses.title: A deadlocked jury led to competing accounts of the holdout
explore_lenses.summary: The challenge follows a mistrial after a jury deadlock, not a conviction or acquittal. The defense says the judge should have investigated complaints that the holdout would not apply the reasonable-doubt instruction; the juror, through counsel, says he was certain Clancy knew what she was doing.

claims.text: Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial on September 4, 2026, after the jury reported it could not reach a unanimous decision; the case therefore returned procedurally to its pretrial posture rather than producing a final verdict.
Clancy’s lawyers argue that the judge should have individually questioned or replaced the holdout after the foreperson raised concerns that a juror was not following the reasonable-doubt instruction.

Holdout juror Michael Desronvil, in a statement released by his lawyer Edward Paltzik, said he had no doubts that Clancy knew what she was doing; he said other jurors cut him off when he tried to discuss theories based on the evidence.

explore_lenses.label: What could happen at the next hearing?
explore_lenses.title: The judge must address records and the case’s future
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate issues are the defense requests to preserve or inspect juror-related material and to dismiss the charges after the mistrial. Separately, prosecutors retain the decision whether to seek a new trial if the case is not dismissed.

claims.text: NBC Boston reported that a hearing on the juror-records motion was scheduled for September 29, 2026, in Plymouth Superior Court.

The defense has also moved to dismiss the case on double-jeopardy grounds, arguing that the mistrial should not have been declared; the Plymouth County District Attorney’s Office had not commented on the motions as of September 21.

Forecast: absent a dismissal or other bar, the prosecution could retry Clancy because a mistrial caused by a deadlocked jury ordinarily leaves charges pending; AP reported prosecutors had not yet said whether they would pursue another trial.

story_report.summary: Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer has asked a judge to investigate the cellphone use and questionnaire responses of the holdout juror after Clancy’s trial ended in a mistrial. The defense seeks the juror’s call and text records during deliberation hours and preservation of court and jury-selection records, but the request does not establish that any improper phone use occurred. A hearing on the records motion was scheduled for Sept. 29 in Plymouth Superior Court, while the case remains unresolved after the deadlocked jury.

sections.heading: Juror Device Rules and Inquiry Limits
sections.body: Massachusetts Trial Court policy generally bars jurors from using phones or other internet-capable devices while attending trial or deliberating. Devices may be used during lunch breaks, provided they are not used to obtain or disclose information about the case. State evidence guidance also limits inquiry into a jury’s internal discussions, votes and mental processes, while allowing examination of whether outside influence or prejudicial outside information improperly affected deliberations.

sections.heading: Competing Accounts of Holdout Juror
sections.body: Clancy’s lawyers contend the judge should have individually questioned or replaced the holdout after the foreperson raised concerns that a juror was not following the reasonable-doubt instruction. The holdout, Michael Desronvil, said through his lawyer that he had no doubt Clancy knew what she was doing and that other jurors cut him off when he tried to discuss theories based on the evidence. Those competing accounts have not been tested through a court-authorized inquiry.

sections.heading: Mistrial Leaves Charges Pending
sections.body: Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial on Sept. 4, 2026, after the jury said it could not reach a unanimous decision, returning the case to its pretrial posture rather than producing a verdict. The defense has separately sought dismissal on double-jeopardy grounds, arguing the mistrial should not have been declared. Unless a dismissal or other legal bar applies, prosecutors could retry Clancy because a deadlocked-jury mistrial ordinarily leaves charges pending.

unresolved.text: The court had not publicly ruled on whether it would authorize the requested juror inquiry or review the requested records.
No public decision had been reported on the defense dismissal motion or on whether prosecutors will seek another trial.

related_stories.title: Typhoon Dujuan Causes Deaths and Destruction in Japan
related_stories.summary: Typhoon Dujuan has resulted in at least four fatalities and 22 injuries in Japan, with reports of six individuals missing. The storm brought record rainfall and violent winds, leading to landslides and significant power outages affecting thousands of homes near Tokyo. As the typhoon moves away, authorities have begun to downgrade heavy rain and landslide warnings.

related_stories.title: Sri Lanka Court Convicts 15 for 2019 Easter Sunday Bombings
related_stories.summary: A Sri Lankan court has convicted 15 individuals for their involvement in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings that targeted three churches and three luxury hotels, resulting in the deaths of 279 people. The attacks were inspired by the Islamic State group and are among the deadliest in the country's history.
